newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Min and Smelt to change wage system - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Min and Smelt to change wage system - paper.

text.p: The workers and management of Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co Ltd have agreed to introduce a new wage system next fiscal year under which profits-related pay hikes will no longer be guaranteed, a Japanese newspaper said on Wednesday.

The new system has been agreed in light of the fact the company is expected to continue to face a difficult business environment in the medium to long term although its earnings are now recovering, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun economic daily said.
The company's move is likely to prompt changes in traditional wage hike negotiations throughout Japanese industry, the paper said.

Japanese companies usually increases employees' monthly salaries once a year and the raise consists of a hike in seniority-based pay and an increase based on the company's performance. At many companies, employees get twice yearly bonuses as well. And Japanese companies' labour unions traditionally hold wage hike negotiations every year.

Under the new system, due to come into effect next April, Mitsui will only guarantee the seniority-based increase, abandoning the profit-based increase in the annual pay review. But it will pay larger bonuses when the company's performance is good, the newspaper said.
Mitsui was not immediately available for comment.
